messages:
evan: Quick ask — can someone run a full onboarding perf sweep for beryl-9b? Need steady-state throughput, p99/p95 tail latency, and an estimated per-1M-token cost with our current quantized runtime. Please include runs with cache enabled/disabled and batch sizes [1,4,8].

maya: On it. I can kick off the smoke then the longer sweep. Do we want KV cache TTL on by default for the sweep? That affects steady-state.

evan: Yes, include both: cache=on (TTL=300s) and cache=off. Also note testing context lengths at 512 and 2048.

asst: infra-bot posted: deploy started for model beryl-9b @ commit f3a9c2 (runtime=quant8, kernels=v2)

sam: Smoke run done (quick numbers):
- batch=1, ctx=512, cache=off: p50=28ms p95=120ms p99=240ms TPS=35
- batch=4, ctx=512, cache=off: p50=30ms p95=130ms p99=260ms TPS=120
I pushed logs to s3:/bench/beryl9b/smoke/2201234567.tar.gz

leo: looks ok for smoke. For the long sweep I recommend enabling the async KV prefetcher flag (+kv_prefetch=true) for the cache=on runs — we saw lower tail latency on similar 9b models. Also watch GPU memory pressure with batch=8 at ctx=2048.

maya: Kicking off full sweep now. Config snippet I used:
```
models: beryl-9b
runtime: quant8
batch_sizes: [1,4,8]
contexts: [512,2048]
cache: [on, off]
kv_prefetch: [true,false]
metrics: [p50,p95,p99,throughput,token_cost]
```

bench-bot: sweep started (run id: sweep-2201234567-01). Estimated runtime 3h 20m.

(3h later)

maya: Sweep finished. Highlights:
- Best throughput: batch=8, ctx=512, cache=on -> 420 TPS (p95 160ms, p99 300ms)
- Lowest tail latency (cache on + kv_prefetch=true): batch=1, ctx=512 -> p99 210ms
- Context=2048 increases p95 ~x1.6 and p99 ~x1.9 across batches (expected)
- Batch=8 at ctx=2048 hit GPU OOM on one node; we retry with smaller microbatching on that node.

sam: I aggregated token cost using current pricing kernel and observed approx $0.90 per 1M tokens for quant8 steady-state with cache on and batch=4. Cost rises ~1.8x with cache off (more tokens computed). Full CSV attached in the s3 folder.

leo: Two callouts from profiling (per-node traces):
- KV cache hit-path shows a 6-8ms tail in CPU serialization before hitting GPU for some requests -> possible batching inefficiency in worker.
- Attention kernel for 2048 sequences uses fallback kernel on older GPU SKU (p99 inflated). We should pin kernel v3 for that SKU or route those requests to a newer pool.

evan: Good notes. Action items:
- maya: rerun batch=8@ctx=2048 with microbatching=2 on the node that OOMed and confirm no correctness drift.
- sam: prepare a short cost/latency summary for PMs with the CSV + bullets.
- leo: open infra ticket to either pin kernel v3 for older GPU SKU or add routing rule. Include perf traces.

maya: Started the microbatch rerun. Quick result: batch=8, ctx=2048, microbatch=2 -> no OOM, p95 ~480ms, p99 ~920ms (was p95 760ms p99 1400ms before).

sam: Drafted summary: 3 slides + table. Will post in this thread and in /doc/product-onboarding/beryl9b.md by EOD.

leo: Infra ticket created: INF-4521. Routing rule suggested: prefer pool-gpu-a (kernel v3) for ctx>=1024 or fallback to quant-microbatching.

evan: Thanks everyone. One follow-up Q: Any signs of semantic/regression drift comparing outputs vs our golden eval? Did we run evals alongside perf?

maya: Yes, ran the golden eval set for 1k prompts after the main sweep — exact match/regression checks passed (no significant logprob diffs). I put eval artifacts next to the bench CSV.

evan: Perfect. I'll close the onboarding ticket once sam posts the PM summary. If anyone wants a quick sync, I'll be around at 3:30 for 15m. :thumbsup:
